required_content.problem: Durable artifacts need continuity across planning, funding, work assignment, release, maintenance, governance, and eventual sunset without turning an AI manager into the owner of the project. Issue trackers, CI systems, bots, DAOs, funding pages, and project-management tools each cover a slice of artifact lifecycle, but none by themselves preserve mission, memory, authority, treasury limits, contributor credit, evidence, and death protocol as one governed project steward.
required_content.core_mechanism: Artifact Steward Agents and Living Project Governance owns a project-, artifact-, mission-, owner-, authority-, roadmap-, work-contract-, event-, treasury-, compute-, contributor-, evidence-, governance-, release-, federation-, sunset-, consumer-, environment-, and time-specific Artifact Steward Continuity Lease: it may observe, propose, prepare, coordinate, execute, reverse, archive, or retire only through a versioned charter, taint-aware intake, scoped work contracts, separated contribution ledgers, bounded treasury and compute policy, verification and release gates, appeal and fork or exit paths, effect-complete rollback, and explicit sunset authority; it never acquires ownership, governance legitimacy, evidence authority, funding rights, release authority, legal standing.
required_content.worked_trace: Seven schema-and-fixture record families; twelve Lean declarations reducing lifecycle, contribution-ledger, and federation route functions; one deterministic public-safe lifecycle probe with two valid routes and six expected-invalid controls; and one adjacent synthetic release evidence-and-approval handoff. Work-contract dispatch and release-gate route targets remain planned rather than being represented by assumption-restating implications. No steward bot, real event intake, treasury or compute executor, contributor service, governance runner, federation harness, protected-branch action, release runner, sunset protocol, natural project workload, independent reproduction, deployment, or chapter-core support effect exists.

Authority laundering converts a helpful proposal, prior approval, role, token, vote, workflow, fixture, theorem, or emergency action into general permission. Workflow injection lets untrusted issue, pull-request, comment, webhook, dependency, artifact, benchmark, or worker text become steward control input. Credential and protected-asset capture exposes branches, releases, registries, domains, keys, wallets, personal data, or external systems beyond the contract.
